packages.label: יִחוּדִים וְזִוּוּגִים וּבִטּוּל אִסּוּר
packages.label_en: Divine Unions, Matchings, and the Nullification of Prohibition
packages.reason: The Rebbe establishes one foundational bechina in this Torah: all yichudim (divine unifications of upper and lower worlds) and all zivugim (marital matchings) are in the nature of biṭṭul isur — the transformation of the forbidden into the permitted. These are not cause and effect; they are two faces of the same spiritual event. A yichud/zivug IS biṭṭul isur — the separation that made something forbidden is dissolved when the two become one. The Rebbe repeats this equation three times (paragraphs 1, 2, 4), confirming it as the central structural claim. Both concepts belong to the same positive, holy domain: the restoration of wholeness, marriage, and unity.

stats.note: Torah LM2/29 is a very compact teaching (4 paragraphs). The entire bechina content is concentrated in one equation: yichud/zivug = biṭṭul isur. The source text discusses halachic concepts (ארוסה, נשואה, שאלה בבית) and verses ('אֱלֹקִים מוֹשִׁיב יְחִידִים בַּיְתָה'), but all of these function as illustrations or proofs for the one bechina equation, not as independent bechina concepts in their own right. There is no explicit evil mirror in this Torah — the negative case (a question that cannot be nullified) is described as a SIGN of damage to a supernal yichud, not as a separate evil package with its own bechina cluster.
